newsitem.title: USA: Bank SinoPac of Taiwan to acquire LA's Far East.
newsitem.headline: Bank SinoPac of Taiwan to acquire LA's Far East.

text.p: Bank SinoPac of Taiwan said Thursday it has a definitive agreement to acquire Far East National Bank of Los Angeles for $85 million to $90 million in cash.
The price will depend on the book value of Far East's 5.67 million outstanding shares at the closing of the transaction. As of June 30, the book value per share was $7.66.
The deal is expected to close during the first half of 1997, subject to the approval of Far East shareholders and regulators.

"Bank SinoPac is committed to international expansion throughout the Pacific Rim, and the acquisition of Far East National Bank represents an important step in that direction," said Bank SinoPac's President, Paul C. Y. Lo.

Founded in 1974, Far East was the first Asian-American federally chartered bank in the continental United States. It has 10 branches in California and an office in Beijing. As of June 30, Far East had assets of $496 million.
Bank SinoPac of Taiwan operates 24 branches in 14 cities throughout Taiwan. The bank has assets of about $4.5 billion.
Far East will delist from the American Stock Exchange, but SinoPac may relist its shares in the future, Lo said in an interview.
Far East closed Wednesday at $13.75 on the Amex.
